title: Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme Inhibitory Assay
author: Francisco Herrera
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.tb4eiqw
materials: Aqueous extract (40 µL) was added to a 20 µL solution of ACE (Sigma) (100 mU/mL), and incubated at 37 °C for 5 min.
The reaction was stopped by adding 360 mL of TT dioxane (Sigma) solution (3% w/v) and 720 mL of 0.2 M phosphate buffer (JT Baker) (pH 8.3).

steps.title: Prepare HHL substrate solution
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of HHL prepared at 0.3 % (w/v) in a mixture containing 40 µmol potassium phosphate buffer (JT Baker, Mexico).

steps.title: Add NaCl buffer and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 300 µM sodium chloride buffer (JT Baker, Center Valley, PA, USA) that has been adjusted to pH 8.3 with either 1 M HCl or 1 M NaOH, then incubate the reaction mixture at 37 °C for 45 min.

substeps.instruction: Adjust buffer pH to 8.3 using 1 M HCl or 1 M NaOH.

steps.title: Centrifuge and measure absorbance
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the reaction mixture at 10,000 × g for 10 min; collect the supernatant and measure its absorbance at 382 nm using a Perkin‑Elmer Lambda XLS UV/VIS spectrophotometer.

steps.title: Repeat assays in triplicate and analyze
steps.instruction: Perform each assay in triplicate, then quantify antihypertensive activity by regression analysis of ACE inhibitory activity (%) versus phenolic compound concentration to determine the IC₅₀ (concentration giving 50 % inhibition).

substeps.instruction: Plot ACE inhibition (%) against phenolic concentration.
Calculate IC₅₀ from the regression curve.

steps.title: Include lisinopril as control
steps.instruction: Use lisinopril (an antihypertensive drug) as a positive control in the ACE inhibitory assay.
